history.answer: Mount Morgan, a gold mine located 36 km south-west of Rockhampton, is recorded as an abandoned mine with a giant size band of over 150 tonnes. Reported production figures vary across sources, including approximately 250 tonnes of gold (8.04 Moz troy) from 1882 to 1990, approximately 360,000 tonnes of copper from 1882 to 1990, and approximately 262 tonnes of gold (8.42 Moz troy) from 1882 to 1981. Other production records include approximately 37 tonnes of silver from 1882 to 1981, approximately 387,000 tonnes of copper from 1882 to 1981, and 294,056 kg of gold (9.45 Moz troy) with an unspecified period. The mine's closure is recorded as 1990 with no reason quoted, or 1981 when operations were scaled back due to the exhaustion of its ore body. Ownership and tenure changed over time, starting with Mount Morgan Gold Mining Company Limited (1886 to 1928), followed by Mount Morgan Limited (1928 to 1990), Peko-Wallsend (from 1968), Norton Gold Fields (from 2007), the Queensland Government (from 1993), and Heritage Minerals Pty Ltd (from 2020).

survey.answer: Mount Morgan (Geological Survey of Queensland site 494270) is recorded as an abandoned mine on the Mount Morgan 1:100,000 sheet (36 km south-west of rockhampton, 90km wnw of gladstone.), at -23.6370, 150.3692, located to within 100 m. The survey classes its gold as giant, over 150 t, and also records copper (large), pyrite (medium), silver (small). Within 5 km it records 37 other historical workings, 36 of them with gold; other commodities nearby: copper, molybdenum, silver. Other records with a similar name: Mount Morgan (479252). The record gives a size band, not production figures, and holds no owners or closure dates.

structured_record.answer: Mount Morgan (GSQ site 494270, 36 km south-west of rockhampton, 90km wnw of gladstone) is recorded by the Geological Survey of Queensland as abandoned mine, gold size band giant, >150 t. Reported production: about 250 tonnes gold, about 8.04 Moz troy (converted here; the survey records 250 t) (1882 to 1990, Mount Morgan mine, per Queensland Government (qld.gov.au)); about 360,000 tonnes copper (1882 to 1990, Mount Morgan mine, per Queensland Government (qld.gov.au)); approximately 262 tonnes gold, about 8.42 Moz troy (converted here; the survey records 262 t) (1882 to 1981, Mount Morgan mine, per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293)); approximately 37 tonnes silver (1882 to 1981, Mount Morgan mine, per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293)); approximately 387,000 tonnes copper (1882 to 1981, Mount Morgan mine, per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293)); 294,056 kg gold, about 9.45 Moz troy (converted here; the survey records 294,056 kg) (period not stated, Mount Morgan, per GSQ MINOCC 2017 (Total_Ores_Prod, SITE_NO 494270)); 36,842 kg silver (period not stated, Mount Morgan, per GSQ MINOCC 2017 (Total_Ores_Prod, SITE_NO 494270)); 360,616 tonnes copper (period not stated, Mount Morgan, per GSQ MINOCC 2017 (Total_Ores_Prod, SITE_NO 494270)); 102,000,000 tonnes ore (period not stated, Mount Morgan, per GSQ MINOCC 2017 (Total_Ores_Prod, SITE_NO 494270)). GSQ MINOCC 2017 also lists 4 dated Production rows (gold: 1,835 kg period not stated; 157,273 kg to 1927; 78,788 kg 1929 to 1982; 56,160 kg 1983 to 1990); see production. Closure: 1990 (no reason quoted) [Mount Morgan mine, unknown, per Queensland Government (qld.gov.au)]; 1981 - "Mount Morgan Limited progressively scaled back its workforce and operations until it reached the end of its ore body in 1981." [Mount Morgan mine, exhausted, per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293)]; 1927 - "The Mount Morgan Gold Mining Company Limited operated using underground mining methods until 1927 when fire destroyed underground workings. The company deliberately flooded its underground workings in response to the fire and went into liquidation." [Mount Morgan Gold Mining Company underground workings, unknown, per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293)]; 1990 (no reason quoted) [Mount Morgan, unknown, per GSQ MINOCC 2017 (MineHist, SITE_NO 494270, row 6)]. Years worked per GSQ MINOCC 2017 (MineHist, SITE_NO 494270): 1882-1903, 1903-(no end year), 1925-1927, 1929-1968, 1968-1981, 1981-1990, 1882-(no end year). Ownership and tenure: Mount Morgan Gold Mining Company Limited (1886 to 1928) per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293); Mount Morgan Limited (1928 to 1990) per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293); Peko-Wallsend (parent of Mount Morgan Limited) (from 1968) per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293); Norton Gold Fields (from 2007) per Wikipedia, Mount Morgan Mine (rev 1368226293); Queensland Government (legacy site management) (from 1993) per Queensland Government (qld.gov.au); Heritage Minerals Pty Ltd (from 2020) per Queensland Government (qld.gov.au); Norton Gold Fields Limited per GSQ MINOCC 2017 (Tenure, SITE_NO 494270); Heritage Minerals Pty Ltd per GA-MINERALDEPOSITS-333486. The recorded figures disagree on production gold (Mount Morgan mine) and production copper (Mount Morgan mine) and closure year (Mount Morgan mine) and production gold, whole-site totals across sources (including MINOCC 2017) and production copper, whole-site totals across sources (including MINOCC 2017) and closure year, whole site, across sources (including MINOCC 2017); every value is kept above, none is merged or chosen. Other GSQ gold sites with the same name (not described here): 479252 (Croydon, very small).
